title: Take logs of both sides before differentiating implicitly (for y = f(x)^g(x) type functions)
content: When a function has a variable in both the base and the exponent (e.g. y = x^x), you cannot differentiate it directly with the power rule. Instead, take ln of both sides to bring the exponent down: ln(y) = x*ln(x). Differentiate implicitly with respect to x, using the product rule on the right-hand side: (1/y)*(dy/dx) = ln(x) + 1. Then multiply both sides by y to get dy/dx = y*(ln(x)+1) = x^x*(1+ln x). This technique is the standard route to stationary points, tangents, or general differentiation of exponential-of-a-function expressions.
